CDISC datasets

Source: vignettes/articles/cdisc.Rmd
cdisc.Rmd

sideview recognises tables that look like SDTM, SEND or ADaM datasets and marks them with a badge. This is for awareness: it helps you see what each card is. It does not check a dataset against an implementation guide, and a table that does not look like CDISC data is left alone.

Everything below uses a small synthetic study built in the page (no real patients).

A synthetic study 

usub <- paste0("SV-001-", sprintf("%03d", 1:4))
sid <- "SV-001"

dm <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, DOMAIN = "DM", USUBJID = usub, SUBJID = sprintf("%03d", 1:4),
                 AGE = c(34, 51, 62, 45), SEX = c("F", "M", "F", "M"),
                 ARM = c("A", "B", "A", "B"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
attr(dm$USUBJID, "label") <- "Unique Subject Identifier"
attr(dm$AGE, "label") <- "Age"
attr(dm, "label") <- "Demographics"

ae <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, DOMAIN = "AE", USUBJID = usub, AESEQ = 1:4,
                 AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash", "Cough"),
                 AESEV = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "MILD", "SEVERE"),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

suppae <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, RDOMAIN = "AE", USUBJID = usub, IDVAR = "AESEQ",
                     IDVARVAL = as.character(1:4), QNAM = "AETRTEM",
                     QLABEL = "Treatment Emergent", QVAL = "Y", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

adsl <- data.frame(STUDYID = sid, USUBJID = usub, TRT01P = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
                   TRT01A = c("A", "B", "A", "B"), AGE = dm$AGE, SAFFL = "Y",
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

Badges 

sideview_widget(dm = dm, ae = ae, suppae = suppae, adsl = adsl)

Each recognised card gets a badge after its name: DM, AE, SUPPAE and ADSL here. Hover over a badge for the dataset label, the standard and class, and the evidence used (for example “DOMAIN column = DM” or “STUDYID + USUBJID”). SUPPAE also says which parent it supplements. Column headers show a variable’s label as a tooltip, L shows a row of labels under the headers (it is saved with the workspace, as view.labels_row), and Ctrl+K finds a card by its domain or dataset label.

The tags are worked out in R when the canvas is built. They are never saved in a workspace file; they are worked out again when it is opened.

Overrides with cdisc =

cdisc is "auto" by default. Turn it off with FALSE, or name the domain of a table that sideview cannot tell on its own:

sideview_widget(my_events = ae, cdisc = FALSE)
sideview_widget(my_events = ae[, -2], cdisc = c(my_events = "AE"))

The same argument is on sideview(), save_sideview(), sideviewServer() and sv_codebook(). In a Shiny module the badges follow sv_add_card(), sv_replace_card() and sv_remove_card().

Domains in the codebook

sv_codebook() gets a domain column, and the widget’s CSV download matches it.

cb <- sv_codebook(dm = dm, ae = ae, adsl = adsl)
unique(cb[, c("table", "domain")])
#>    table domain
#> 1     dm     DM
#> 8     ae     AE
#> 14  adsl   ADSL

With cdisc = FALSE the column is NA.

The catalogue 

cdisc_cat <- sv_cdisc_catalogue()
head(cdisc_cat[, 1:min(5, ncol(cdisc_cat))])
#>   name                      label           class standard ig_versions
#> 1   DM               Demographics Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 2   CO                   Comments Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 3   SE           Subject Elements Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 4   SV             Subject Visits Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 5   SM Subject Disease Milestones Special-Purpose     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4
#> 6   AG           Procedure Agents   Interventions     SDTM 3.2;3.3;3.4

The catalogue lists the datasets sideview knows. Its ig_versions column (implementation guide versions) is approximate. It exists so badges can say what a table is, not to validate it.

Reading CDISC files

sv_read_cdisc() reads a folder, or a set of files, of .xpt, .sas7bdat, Dataset-JSON (.json) and .parquet into a named list, keeping variable labels. Names are the lower-case file stems. It needs the package for each format (haven, datasetjson, arrow), and it never uses the network.

study <- sv_read_cdisc("study/sdtm")
sideview_widget(study)

Parquet files stay on disk as Arrow Datasets unless you pass lazy = FALSE.

Join keys

Tagged tables join on known keys. With the tables above on the canvas, Auto Map (gadget or Shiny module) suggests them as dashed splines, drawn as one group per join:

sideview(dm = dm, ae = ae, adsl = adsl)
Pair Keys Kind
adae to ae STUDYID, USUBJID, AESEQ ADaM to SDTM trace
ae to dm, adlb to adsl STUDYID, USUBJID subject level (the hub is the lookup)
lb to sv STUDYID, USUBJID, VISITNUM visit level

An SDTM or SEND table links to DM; an ADaM table links to ADSL (the other hub is used when the preferred one is not on the canvas). Hover one spline and the whole group lights up. A click accepts all of it as one left_join, and one undo takes it back. A partial key set is never offered. Without a STUDYID column the subject key is USUBJID alone, and the suggestion’s reason says so.

The rules are also available as a function, and sv_suggest_mappings() returns them first, with group and kind columns:

sv_suggest_mappings(list(dm = dm, ae = ae, adsl = adsl))[, c("from_table", "to_table", "from_col", "to_col", "kind")]
#>   from_table to_table from_col  to_col    kind
#> 1         ae       dm  STUDYID STUDYID subject
#> 2         ae       dm  USUBJID USUBJID subject
#> 3       adsl       dm  STUDYID STUDYID subject
#> 4       adsl       dm  USUBJID USUBJID subject

Key checks

Open the join check on a join between two tagged tables and a CDISC list appears below the usual warnings. It names a key the join lacks (Add AESEQ: the CDISC key for adae and ae is STUDYID, USUBJID, AESEQ.), explains a many-to-many join with no rule (two Findings tables such as LB and VS should be filtered to one test, or summarised, first) and warns when a natural key repeats. The notes use the catalogue and the counts already in the check, so they cost no extra pass over the data, and they work for arrow and duckdb cards too. They do not change what Strict writes.

What join keys do not do

  • RELREC tables, and tables without USUBJID (TS, TA, TE), are not suggested. SUPP-- tables are merged, not joined (see the next section), so they are left out of the join suggestions above.
  • Sponsor sequence names other than <D>SEQ are not traced; those pairs get the subject rule.
  • Findings with findings (LB with VS) get a note, not a suggestion.
  • The widget has no Auto Map rules and no notes; they are worked out in R, in the gadget and in modules.
  • cdisc = FALSE turns both off.

Merging SUPP– tables

A supplemental qualifier table (SUPPAE, SUPPDM, or the generic SUPPQUAL) holds one row per qualifier: QNAM names the variable, QVAL is its value, and USUBJID, IDVAR and IDVARVAL say which parent record it belongs to. A plain join would multiply the parent rows by the number of qualifiers, so sideview folds the rows into the parent instead: one new column per QNAM, with its QLABEL as the column label.

On a tagged SUPPAE card, the Merge into AE button adds a merge step to the Pipeline tab. Auto Map offers the same thing as a dashed spline group from the SUPP card to its parent. Pressing the button again replaces the step with a fresh plan, and one undo takes it back.

The step writes tidyr + dplyr code. When the step is added, sideview records a plan (the type of the key, the IDVAR levels and the QNAMs) and writes it into the code, together with guards that stop the code if the data no longer fits the plan.

The merge check

sv_supp_check() is the check behind the button. It runs on the study above:

chk <- sv_supp_check(ae, suppae, parent_name = "ae", supp_name = "suppae")
chk$status
#> [1] "ok"
c(parent = chk$n_parent, supp = chk$n_supp, matched = chk$n_matched, orphan = chk$n_orphan)
#>  parent    supp matched  orphan 
#>       4       4       4       0
chk$columns
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$name
#> [1] "AETRTEM"
#> 
#> [[1]]$label
#> [1] "Treatment Emergent"

The same report is shown at the top of the Discrepancy tab (and on the step line in the Pipeline tab):

  • counts of parent rows, SUPP rows, matched rows, orphans (SUPP rows that match no parent record, with samples) and rows of other RDOMAINs;
  • problems: a QNAM that repeats for one record, a QNAM that clashes with a parent column or sits at two IDVAR levels, and IDVARVAL values that do not convert to the parent’s key type (counted apart from orphans);
  • the new columns with their labels, and a preview of the merged parent.

The status is error when the code would stop (repeats, clashes, two-level QNAMs, an unsupported key type), warning for orphans and bad IDVARVALs, and ok otherwise. A step with an error is still added so that you can read the report; its step line says that it stops. When a re-check finds that the data no longer fits the plan (an edited suppae, say), the step line reads “Merge needs refreshing” and Refresh takes the plan that re-check found, as one undo step. Refresh runs no check of its own.

With an arrow or duckdb parent, the parent stays lazy: only the SUPP table is collected. With an arrow parent the code casts a numeric key to the parent’s own Arrow type, so an int64 AESEQ from a parquet file joins. In the widget the check runs in the browser on the embedded rows; when a card’s rows were cut (max_rows) or the card is lazy, the panel says “Preview rows”.

What it does not do

  • The ig_versions in the catalogue are approximate, and nothing is validated against an implementation guide.
  • A table named AD... (ADLB, ADAE, ADVS) is tagged ADaM when its columns confirm an ADaM structure, even if it keeps SDTM-prefixed columns such as LBTESTCD; the tooltip records the prefix as a disagreement. With any other name, SDTM-prefixed columns still give an SDTM tag.
  • Column names are matched whatever their case (STUDYID, studyid), but a STUDYID column is still required for tagging. The SUPP merge is stricter: it needs the exact upper-case names USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM and QVAL (and STUDYID, RDOMAIN and QLABEL when present).
  • There is no hard limit on merges, but the checks are uneven. A second merge into one parent (a SUPPAE and a SUPPQUAL) is checked in the browser, where a QNAM already made by an earlier merge, mutate or rename counts as a clash. The guard inside the generated code looks only at the source parent table, so after an earlier join, summarise, pivot or custom step the browser cannot see the chain’s columns either, and dplyr would add .x/.y suffixes instead of stopping.
  • The check runs when you press the Merge button, when you open the step line or the report, after opening a workspace, after undo or redo, and after a module card is replaced or removed. Refresh runs no check, and nothing checks when the code runs: if the data change later, only the guards in the generated code stop a rerun on new data.
  • IDVARVAL is matched after conversion to the key type. The in-memory R check compares a double key as 15 significant digits of text, while the generated code and the lazy duckdb check compare the doubles themselves, and the browser reads the shortest round-trip text. So for a double key with more than 15 significant digits the gadget’s own report can disagree with its code, and the gadget with the widget. A key that does not look like a plain decimal ("0x10", "Inf", "1d3") is counted as a bad IDVARVAL.
  • cdisc = FALSE shows no tags, but lazy (arrow / duckdb) cards still run detection when they are built. A named cdisc = vector with several lazy cards gets slower with each verb.
  • Dataset-JSON reading was checked against datasetjson 0.4.1; if a file’s structure differs, it is skipped with a warning.
  • The Copilot gets column labels and a domain line as schema text, never row data.
  • The label row is placed from one measurement of the header height, so it could sit off if a header grows taller later.
  • The interface was checked in headless Chrome and by hand in RStudio’s dialog and Viewer pane. In an external browser the canvas was seen to load, but its interaction was covered only by the headless Chrome tests (see the log for the release).
